summary.name: Drifting
summary.one_liner: Drifting is a free, open-source, local-first novel writing app for Mac and Windows that combines a Markdown-style editor, chapter and outline tools, and an AI Agent that can read and edit the whole manuscript.
use_cases: Drafting a novel chapter by chapter
Tracking characters, places and lore for a book
Planning storylines and a plot grid per chapter
Editing a manuscript as a folder of Markdown files in Obsidian
Exporting a finished book to EPUB, PDF or Word
Using an AI agent to file notes into story elements
summary.what_it_does: Drifting is a writing app where each project is also a folder of Markdown files, and it supports Markdown shortcuts while typing and imports .md, .txt and .docx. It organizes a book into chapters, with elements for characters, places, objects and lore, storylines, a timeline in book order or narrative time, and a plot grid per chapter. An optional AI Agent, using the user's own DeepSeek, Anthropic or OpenAI key (or an experimental ChatGPT subscription), can read, search and edit the project and marks its edits so they can be undone. Projects can be exported as EPUB, PDF, Word or Markdown ZIP, and the whole library can be backed up as a .drifting file.
notable: Open source under AGPL-3.0-or-later, buildable from GitHub
Local-first: works offline with no account; manuscripts stored as Markdown files
AI Agent for the whole project, with edits marked in text and undoable; writing never requires AI
Codex, Claude Code and Antigravity can connect via MCP, read-only by default
caveats: Early development; keep independent copies of manuscripts that matter
Windows support is a preview; macOS requires 13 or later on Apple Silicon
Agent needs an online model service; local models are not supported yet; sync between computers requires an account and is not end-to-end encrypted
